prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 2 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 2 panels across and 1 down, read left to right. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Modern Hotel Operations Office; image 2 is the approved last panel of the previous part of this scene's board. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: panel 1 of this sheet, repeated exactly: the same camera, place, light and mannequins.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the red mannequin; Company B Operations Manager is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one cohesive storyboard sheet, four columns by three rows, with ten panels ordered left to right and top to bottom; leave the final two cells empty and unframed. Use smooth colour-coded artist's mannequins: Company B Operations Manager is blue, medium-tall and lean; Company A Operations Manager is red, medium-height with an average build. People are represented only through body pose and head direction. Render the office and props realistically: cream walls, pale oak furniture, dark task chairs, flush timber cupboards, glazed partitions and a matte-black widescreen desktop computer with a compact keyboard and mouse. Steady dry daytime weather, soft daylight from the window at camera left, warm recessed ceiling lighting, warm-neutral 4800K balance, restrained ivory and honey colours, and clean midtones remain consistent. Keep the office background slightly darker than the subjects. All software graphics are flat, using off-white, charcoal, grey and restrained teal. Draw no lettering, numerals, logos, captions, panel labels or arrows anywhere; represent interface information with unlettered blocks, bars and simple icons.

Geography: The action stays at one pale-oak workstation in the hotel office. The blue host stands at its left end facing screen right, and the red visitor stands at its right end facing screen left, with the monitor between them and its display angled into their shared viewing space. The room-side camera positions remain on the same side of their conversational axis. Looking inward from this side, the broad window and outdoor trees lie toward frame left, timber cupboards occupy the rear centre, and the glazed partition lies toward frame right. The host singles tighten toward the left end of the workstation; the visitor single tightens toward the right end. Screen inserts use a neutral, straight-on position directly in front of this same monitor, lower than the standing cameras. The monitor's narrow black bezel, a sliver of pale-oak desktop and a soft window-light strip at frame left connect the wider office views to these inserts; neither manager changes position.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Same standing head-height host setup, approximately 1.6 metres, from the room side of the axis; chest-up medium close-up, 65mm feel. Background: The window-light strip remains at frame left, soft timber cupboard surfaces remain centre-right, and the same monitor bezel enters at lower right. The blue mannequin stands frame left with its chest facing screen right and its head held three-quarter toward the visitor off frame right. Its torso remains upright and both hands stay below the lower crop. The black computer edge remains at the lower-right corner, with the display itself outside the frame.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing head height, approximately 1.55 metres, from the room side of the same axis; chest-up medium close-up, 65mm feel, looking toward the visitor at the right end of the desk. Background: Soft timber cupboard surfaces lie toward frame left and centre, while the glazed partition and its dark vertical framing occupy frame right. The workstation's black monitor bezel enters at the lower-left edge. The red mannequin occupies frame right with its chest facing screen left and its head turned three-quarter toward the host off frame left. Its head is level, shoulders relaxed and both hands below the lower crop. The same computer bezel appears at lower left without its display entering the frame.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
